html:
The Paaruntyi are an Aboriginal Australian people of northwestern New South Wales, in the Paroo River country north of the Darling.

They are not to be confused with the Barindji further south, who called them "the spitting people". Their speech was a dialect of Paakantyi, the language of the Barkindji. Neighbours included the Gunu to the east and the Karenggapa to the west. Little more is recorded. Sheep and cattle stations reached the Paroo in the 1860s.
sum: The Paaruntyi are an Aboriginal Australian people of northwestern New South Wales, in the Paroo River country north of the Darling.
